current_answer: As of 30 September 2026, public evidence reviewed here still does not establish a broad decline in deployed popular models’ core capability. Check provider status and the affected surface before switching. catalogue_card.question: Were yesterday’s ChatGPT and Claude failures the same problem?
catalogue_card.text: No public evidence shows a shared cause: Claude’s stated impact ended at 14:59 UTC; OpenAI’s incident began at 17:52. The latest OpenAI updates said two 30 September services had recovered. These are service reports, not proof of a model downgrade.

summary: No broad decline in deployed popular models’ core capability is established by the public evidence reviewed here.
Anthropic reported a Claude service-error window on 29 September from 14:00 to 14:59 UTC; its status entry was marked resolved at 16:27 UTC.

OpenAI recorded a separate ChatGPT, Codex, and API incident from 17:52 to 23:14 UTC on 29 September, with failed requests, login trouble, and incomplete tasks. It said an RCA would follow within five business days.
OpenAI’s latest 30 September updates at 10:34 and 10:36 UTC said Space Pages and Pro/Plus services had recovered; both remained under monitoring.
The records show service and product-surface problems, not a repeated test of valid response quality or a shared cause across providers.
Check status, preserve the failed request and task artifact, then replay the same task after recovery with model, route, plan, and settings recorded.
uncertainty: OpenAI had not published the root-cause analysis for its 29 September multi-surface incident at the latest check.
Separate incident windows do not establish whether the providers shared an upstream dependency.
The OpenAI status feed last updated the Pro/Plus and Space Pages reports at 10:36 and 10:34 UTC; individual accounts may differ.
Provider status entries are not model-quality measurements and do not report a representative user denominator.
No representative user sample, same-model longitudinal consumer test, first-party pool analytics, or controlled audience pilot is available.
freshness_note: Checked 30 September 2026. Provider records show separate Claude and OpenAI service incidents on 29 September and OpenAI recovery updates on 30 September. No public repeated-task evidence establishes broad decline in deployed-model capability.
